findings.title: Use the booking organizer's credentials to update the calendar
findings.body: The handler permits attendees to add guests, but constructs EventManager using the caller and the caller's credentials rather than booking.user. For an attendee with no calendar credentials, the organizer's event cannot be updated; an attendee's own credentials likewise do not authorize updates to the organizer's event references. Guests can therefore be saved and emailed without being added to the actual calendar event. Resolve the calendar credentials from the booking organizer.

findings.title: Make failed calendar updates recoverable on retry
findings.body: The attendee insertion has already committed when updateCalendarAttendees is awaited. If that update throws, the mutation fails before sending notifications, but the new attendees remain saved. Retrying the same guest list then removes every address as already present and returns BAD_REQUEST before attempting the calendar update or emails again. A transient integration failure thus leaves an inconsistent booking that this action cannot repair. Make retries complete missing side effects or otherwise recover the failed operation.

findings.title: Authorize team admins or owners rather than requiring both
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines the admin and owner checks with &&. A team admin who is not the owner, organizer, or attendee fails authorization even though the handler explicitly intends to grant team administrators access. Use a disjunction so either authorized team role can add guests.

findings.title: Enforce guest uniqueness on the server
findings.body: uniqueGuests only filters addresses against existing attendees; it does not deduplicate the submitted array. The server schema accepts repeated addresses, so a direct request containing ["new@example.com", "new@example.com"] passes both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees and duplicate notifications. The dialog's uniqueness validation does not protect the API. Validate or deduplicate guest addresses server-side before insertion.

findings.title: Normalize guest addresses before checking the blacklist
findings.body: The configured blacklist is lowercased, but each submitted guest address is compared without normalization. If blocked@example.com is blacklisted, submitting Blocked@example.com passes email validation and bypasses this exclusion, allowing an invitation to the blocked address. Normalize the submitted address before comparing it with the blacklist.

findings.title: Check booking status before sending confirmed invitations
findings.body: The handler never checks booking.status, so an authorized caller can add guests to pending, rejected, or cancelled bookings. sendAddGuestsEmails then sends scheduled invitations to new guests and REQUEST attachments with status CONFIRMED to existing participants. This announces an accepted meeting even when it was never approved or has been cancelled, and can recreate a cancelled calendar invitation. Reject inappropriate booking states or send notifications reflecting the actual status.

findings.title: Respect disabled standard-email settings when adding guests
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and attendees and does not accept event-type metadata. Unlike the existing scheduled, rescheduled, and location-change senders, it therefore ignores disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest sends standard notifications even for event types whose owners explicitly disabled them. Pass the booking's event-type metadata and apply the existing host and attendee disable checks.

findings.title: Populate team members when constructing the calendar event
findings.body: The generated CalendarEvent never includes team information, even for collective bookings with multiple hosts. sendAddGuestsEmails only sends co-host notifications through calendarEvent.team.members, so that branch is always skipped for this handler and hosts other than booking.user are not notified about added guests. Load and populate the booking's participating team members before sending the update.
